prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The bright crop leaves occupy the lower foreground, mostly within about 0.2–1 m of the camera wearer, while the dark upper field, trees, and sky are several metres to the horizon away. The crouching person is generally about 2–4 m ahead; nearby sacks appear roughly 3–7 m away, and the distant animal is approximately 8–15 m away and behind the person. Across the five frames, the person shifts from the right edge to the left, then toward the centre and finally the right again, with modest scale changes suggesting camera turning and some approach in the last frame rather than a clear continuous retreat or approach. The map makes foreground clearance and depth layering clearer than RGB, but its metric distances are only rough, it merges adjacent leaves into smooth surfaces, and it gives unreliable depth around silhouettes, frame edges, the dark-clothed person, and distant objects.
descriptions.segmentation: The map consistently isolates one crouching person ahead of the camera, partly cut off at the right edge in frame 1, partly cut off at the left in frame 2, centred in frames 3–4, and near the upper-right edge in frame 5; the person is roughly 2–4 m away and appears oriented generally toward the camera, although eye direction is not resolved. A cow is marked to the right of and behind the person in frames 2–3, likely about 8–15 m from the camera and several metres from the person; the small cyan “person” detection near the right edge of frame 2 does not match a clear person in RGB and is probably erroneous. The masks clarify which separated image regions belong to the person and reveal edge occlusion, but they omit the crops, sacks, irrigation line, trees, and most other scene structure, so they cannot establish what is within arm's reach except by comparison with RGB. Mask boundaries and labels are unreliable where the person is cropped, and the cow detections are tiny and spatially imprecise.
descriptions.pose: Yellow body keypoints are detected only for the crouching person in frames 3 and 4, placing them roughly 2–4 m in front of the camera and above the near crop bed in image coordinates; no distinct hand keypoints are visible. The compact bent skeletons support a crouched posture with arms held low and forward, with the frame-4 skeleton slightly wider, but they do not reliably determine gaze or whether the torso faces directly toward the camera. No skeleton appears in frames 1, 2, or 5 despite the visible person, so the map cannot track the full left-to-right image movement, the edge occlusions, or any reliable approach or retreat across all five frames. Pose adds joint-level body geometry that is difficult to see against clothing in RGB, but missing legs, sparse joints, absent hands, and unstable limb connections make arm's-reach, orientation, and inter-object distances unreliable.
